gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a flash only widens its zoom for a dome if it can detect the dome: Nikon's SB-5000 senses its own Diffusion Dome and sets the zoom head to 12, 14 or 17 mm on FX (8, 10 or 11 mm on DX). The Godox V1 manual says nothing about detecting accessories, and its zoom only goes down to 28 mm.
standout_why: I compared against the cited B&H AK-R11 spec page (403, unreadable) and against cameraegg.org's 'Best Diffuser for Godox V1 Flash' (2026-10-09), the only rival I could read. Cameraegg covers mounts (four magnetic strips on the AK-R11, slip-on vs magnetic on the AK-R22), spread (180°), dome sizes (12 cm and 15 cm) and prices. It says it has no light-loss figure. It never mentions the zoom setting or bounce, and it doesn't say whether the flash adjusts itself when a dome goes on. ChatGPT's answer has one line saying a small diffuser 'spreads light' and that bouncing off a ceiling is softer, with no maker source.
decides: This confirms how the plan works more than it changes the pick. A dome only softens light by spreading it wide and bouncing it off nearby surfaces. Nikon's own manual pairs the dome with bounce flash ('can be further diffused during bounce flash photography') and says the flash zooms to its widest setting by itself when the dome is fitted. On a Godox V1 with an AK-R11, the flash doesn't do this, so the shopper should set the zoom to 28 mm with the ZOOM button and point the head up or to the side. If they leave auto zoom on, the flash follows the lens focal length and sends a narrower beam into the dome. For a shopper who wants it to just work, a system flash that ships with its own dome and senses it (the Nikon SB-5000 with its SW-15H) is the hands-off choice. A Godox V1 plus AK-R11 does the same job at much lower cost but needs that manual step.
candidates: Nikon SB-5000 + Nikon SW-15H Diffusion Dome

findings.label: Zoom head setting when the Nikon Diffusion Dome is attached
findings.value: Set automatically to 12 mm, 14 mm or 17 mm (FX) or 8 mm, 10 mm or 11 mm (DX), depending on the camera's image area and illumination pattern
findings.source_title: Nikon SB-5000 Reference Manual, page 136 (Nikon Diffusion Dome)
findings.note: Quote: 'the zoom head position is automatically set depending on the camera's image area and illumination pattern.' This is ManualsLib's copy of Nikon's reference manual. I also opened Nikon's own PDF (https://download.nikonimglib.com/archive2/93dVb00nmrTX02Bc5E6323LWcP45/SB-5000RM_(En)01.pdf), but its text layer wouldn't decode in my fetch tool, so the quote is from the mirror.

findings.label: What Nikon says the dome is for
findings.value: Light 'can be further diffused during bounce flash photography', giving 'extremely soft light with virtually no shadow'. Light 'is more effectively diffused when the built-in wide panel is used'
findings.source_title: Nikon SB-5000 Reference Manual, page 136 (Nikon Diffusion Dome)
findings.note: Nikon pitches the dome as an add-on for bounce flash, not as a softener for a flash pointed straight at the subject.

findings.label: Dome and wide panel are separate rows in Nikon's output tables
findings.value: 'BA: With the Nikon Diffusion Dome attached'; 'WP: With the built-in wide panel in place'
findings.note: Nikon gives separate guide numbers for the dome configuration. I didn't extract the guide-number values themselves.

findings.label: Zoom range and how it is set
findings.value: 28–105 mm. Auto zoom sets the coverage 'to match the lens focal length and image size'. Manual zoom is set with the ZOOM button
findings.source_title: Godox V1 TTL Li-ion Round Head Camera Flash Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Nothing in the manual says the V1 detects an attached accessory or changes its zoom when one is fitted. The AK-R1 kit appears only as a separately sold 'accessory kit for round flash head'. The widest V1 setting (28 mm) is narrower than the 12–17 mm the SB-5000 picks for itself with its dome.

findings.label: Heat limit (relevant when firing a lot into a dome at full power)
findings.value: No more than 30 continuous flashes at 1/1 full power, then a rest of at least 10 minutes. Over-temperature protection may kick in after 15 consecutive high-speed-sync flashes
findings.source_title: Godox V1 TTL Li-ion Round Head Camera Flash Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Quoted from the manual's cautions. The manual doesn't connect this limit to diffuser use.

unsourced: How much light the Godox AK-R11 or Nikon SW-15H costs, in stops. Cameraegg says Godox doesn't publish a figure, and I found none in either maker's manual.
